plate.narration: At the last tree, the road gives out. Old steps zigzag toward the red glow; loose stones offer another climb. Below, a traveler hurries downhill. Above, the mountain waits for an answer.

objectives.label: Got the restless bones to lie back down
Surprised the Seal-Keeper, which almost never happens

goal.text: Climb the mountain everyone else is running from, and give your answer.

steps.label: Climb up to the mountain's shoulder
Answer every question you are asked

facet_keystone.name: The Keystone
facet_keystone.text: The crown of the seal under Mount Red Sky. Bigger than your head, warm as a sleeping cat.

scene_tree_line.narration: The last tree on the mountain has a sign nailed to it: NO ROAD BEYOND THIS POINT. SERIOUSLY. Above it, Mount Red Sky glows at the top like a lamp somebody forgot to turn off. Everyone else is running from this mountain. You are going to climb it, find the seal deep inside, and give your answer to whatever is waking under it. Two ways go up: an old zigzag stair, or a slope of loose stones.

variants.text: Back at Redspire, Pellam wrote down what you are here for: to put the stones back, every one.
Back at Redspire, Pellam wrote down what you are here for: to finish the collection, with the stone at the top.
Back at Redspire, Pellam wrote down what you are here for: to take the leash on what sleeps under the mountain.

choices.label: Climb the old zigzag stair, all of it
Scramble straight up the loose stones
Fly up ahead and pick the best way
Sing the Spiral Verses and let the path curl

check_stair.prompt: Climb all four hundred zigzag steps without stopping

onSuccess.narration: Left, right, left, right, four hundred times. Every hundredth step has a tiny carved dragonling face, each one more tired than the last. You never stop once.

onFailure.narration: You stop on every hundredth step, beside a tiny carved dragonling face as tired as you are. It takes ages. But the top is much closer now.

check_scree.prompt: Scramble straight up the loose, sliding stones

onSuccess.narration: You go up like mountain goats, and the stones only slide where you just were. At the top you look down at the long zigzag stair and feel extremely smug.

onFailure.narration: The slope slides, and you slide with it, like a sled, right onto the old stair halfway up. That was not the plan. It works anyway.

scene_tree_line_fly.narration: You flap up over the mountain's shoulder, where the air is warm and smells of struck matches. From up here you can see the best way: a goat track nobody else noticed, hiding behind a big rock shaped like a sleeping cow. You land, point, and lead the way up it, trying very hard not to look pleased with yourself.

choices.label: Up the goat track

scene_tree_line_verses.narration: You sing the Spiral Verses in order, the way the relay taught them, and the path does a strange thing. It curls. Around a boulder, up a gully, past a ledge you would never have found, always gently uphill. Maybe the song was never really about the roads. Maybe it was about getting where the stones are going.

choices.label: Follow the curling path

scene_faun_family.narration: On the first slope, a faun family trots downhill with everything they own, including a goat. The smallest, Tansy, holds out a tiny pink stone. "It hums at night," she whispers. "It hummed louder when the ground shook. Is it my fault?" She wants you to tell her what to do.

variants.text: You check your packs one more time: a few humming rush gems, and nothing else. You came anyway. That is the whole point.
You check your packs one more time. Down among the rush gems: {facets} of the great stones.
You check your packs one more time, and they clank: {facets} great stones. A shower of pebbles rattles down to meet you, like the mountain clearing its throat.

choices.label: Promise to carry it up and put it back for her
Tell her it is only saying hello, and let her keep it
Show her the ford witch's sock trick

scene_faun_family_carry.narration: Tansy puts the stone in your hand and folds your fingers over it, very seriously, like signing a contract. "Tell it sorry from me," she says. Then her family is off downhill, the goat complaining the whole way.

choices.label: Climb on, carrying it

scene_faun_family_hello.narration: "It is only saying hello," you tell her. "Stones do that up here." Tansy holds it to her ear, and her whole face lights up. "Hello," she whispers back. Then she trots off after her family. The goat gives you a long look. It is not convinced.

choices.label: Wave goodbye and climb on

scene_faun_family_sock.narration: You show her how the ford witch kept the Ford Stone: wrapped up snug in a thick wool sock, and kept warm. Tansy's mother pulls a sock out of a bundle at once. It is a very loud sock, striped orange and green. The pink stone goes in, and its hum goes soft as a purr. Tansy hugs the sock, and the family trots on downhill.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_wolf_ledge.narration: The path squeezes along a narrow ledge, and a pack of cinder wolves is lying across it, resting on the only warm rock. Nobody is growling. They look like dogs who have heard thunder and are pretending they have not. The biggest one opens one ember-colored eye.

choices.label: Tiptoe past along the cliff edge
Sit with them a minute, like with a worried dog
Give the big wolf a proper manticore nod
Let the Pride Stone hum, and see if they move
Have a duskrunner scout the ledge and lead the way

check_wolf_ledge.prompt: Tiptoe along the cliff edge past a pack of sleepy wolves

onSuccess.narration: Not one wolf wakes up. Well, one does, but only to roll over with all four paws in the air. You step over the paws, holding your breath, and you are past.

onFailure.narration: A pebble clatters off the edge, and every wolf looks up. The big one sighs and shuffles over to make room, like a grandpa on a crowded bench. You squeeze past, saying sorry to each wolf.

scene_wolf_ledge_sit.narration: You sit down on the warm rock with them. The big wolf leans on you, heavy and toasty as a stove. Every time the ground shakes, the whole pack shivers, and so do you. When you go, the wolves walk you to the end of the ledge, and no further.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_wolf_ledge_nod.narration: You give the big wolf the nod: chin down, tail still, one hunter to another, very proper. The big wolf looks at you for a long moment. Then it nods back, gets up, and leads the whole pack off the ledge in single file so you can pass. The smallest wolf stares at your tail the whole way. Professional courtesy is old, and it still works.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_wolf_ledge_pride.narration: You let the Pride Stone hum in your pack. The wolves' ears go flat. One by one they get up and slink off the ledge into the rocks, the same way the prides would never den near it. The way is clear. It is also very quiet, and the warm rock is empty, and you are not sure you like being the thing that wolves get out of the way of.

choices.label: Climb on, a bit quieter

scene_warden_post.narration: Higher up is the wardens' last post, and it is empty. On the table is a logbook and a very neat sign: ALL CLIMBERS MUST SIGN IN. Under it, a smaller sign: THIS MEANS YOU. Beside the log sits a little box labeled FOR CLIMBERS WHO SIGNED. Beside the box sits a dented tin with a slot in the lid: FOR THE NEXT ONES UP. ONE COIN, PLEASE.

variants.text: You told the wardens everything at Redspire. At the top of today's page it already says: THE ONES WHO TOLD US. PLEASE SIGN BELOW.
A tiny grandmothers' bell is tied to the pencil string. The news you took to the dragonling towns got here before you did.
Nobody up here knows you are coming, and the empty post keeps your secret too.

choices.label: Sign in properly, in your very best writing
Sign in as Sir Pancake and the Cookie Twins
Find tag 4117 in the log, and write FOUND
Leave the wardens a note: we went up
Drop a coin in the tin, for the next ones up

scene_warden_post_sign.narration: You sign in properly, in your best writing. Under WHERE TO you write: the bottom. The little box clicks open. Inside is a warden's mosslight jar, glowing green, labeled FOR THE WAY DOWN. Somebody thought about you getting back.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_warden_post_silly.narration: You sign in as Sir Pancake and the Cookie Twins, and under REASON FOR CLIMB you write: snacks. You laugh so hard that the next steep bit goes by without anybody noticing. The little box stays shut. It is a warden box. It knows.

choices.label: Climb on, still laughing

scene_warden_post_clerks.narration: You flip back through the log until you find it: TAG 4117. STATUS: MISSING. Underlined three times. Somebody has been very upset about tag 4117. You take the pencil on its string and, next to MISSING, you write: FOUND, AND GOING HOME. The little box clicks open for that, too. Inside is a mosslight jar, glowing green, labeled FOR THE WAY DOWN.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_warden_post_note.narration: You tear a page from the back of the log and write: To the wardens. We went up. You know what for. You fold it into a warden-neat square and set it on top of the log, exactly straight, where a warden will look first. It feels like keeping a promise to people who keep all of theirs. The little box clicks open. Inside is a mosslight jar, glowing green.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_overlook.narration: At the mountain's shoulder the clouds pull apart, and you can see the whole realm: the city where you started, the fields, the river roads and the forest roads, all winding north to here. Tiny lights crawl along every one of them, going the other way.

choices.label: Find home, all the way south
Don't look back. Look up.
Find the Great River, all the way down
Find the caravan road, and hum the relay-song
Find the forest, and MossHome inside it

scene_overlook_home.narration: You find it: a smudge far to the south, the size of your thumbnail. Somebody there is probably having dinner. Nobody says anything for a while, which is exactly the right thing to say. Then you turn around.

choices.label: Turn around and climb

scene_overlook_up.narration: You turn your back on all of it and look up. The summit glows red at the edges like a coal somebody just blew on. "Nobody look back," somebody says. Then everybody looks back, just once, very quickly. Everybody agrees that still counts.

variants.text: You turn your back on all of it and look up. The summit glows red at the edges like a coal somebody just blew on. "Don't look back," you tell yourself, out loud. Then you look back, just once, very quickly. You decide that still counts.

choices.label: Climb

scene_overlook_river.narration: You find the Great River, a silver ribbon running all the way down the realm, and on it a tiny dot that might be a flat boat with a frog in a very old hat. It is much too far to be sure. But the dot stops moving, the way a boat would stop if somebody on it had just looked up a mountain. Then it drifts on downstream.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_overlook_rush.narration: You find the caravan road, the busiest road in the realm, and you hum the relay-song down at it. It is a very long way down. But a moment later, faint as a whisper, the next line comes floating back up on the wind, sung by a hundred travelers all going the other way. The relay never stops. Not even now. Not even for this.

choices.label: Climb on, humming

scene_overlook_wild.narration: You find the forest, a dark green blanket over half the realm, and somewhere in the middle of it, MossHome. As you look, the whole forest sways at once, every tree together, like a crowd waving. It is probably the wind. It is probably not the wind. You wave back, just in case, and a little way down the slope a raven pretends not to have seen.

choices.label: Climb on

choice_cairn.narration: Near the top stands a cairn: a tall pile of stones, each one left by somebody who climbed this far. Some have names on them. One is wearing a tiny knitted hat. The rule is that you leave something before the last climb. Everybody vote: what do we leave?

choices.label: A pebble with every name in the party on it
A pebble with a secret wish whispered into it
Our last snack, for whoever climbs up next
Our names, carved as BIG as they will go
Read the very oldest stone first

choice_cairn_names.narration: You scratch your names onto a pebble and set it near the top. It looks very small among all the other names. But it will still be there tomorrow, whatever happens. The pile creaks, as if making room.

variants.text: You scratch your name onto a pebble and set it near the top. It looks very small among all the other names. But it will still be there tomorrow, whatever happens down below. The pile creaks a little, making room for exactly one more.

choices.label: Climb on

choice_cairn_wish.narration: You whisper wishes into the same pebble, taking turns, and nobody tells anybody what they wished. For a moment the pebble feels warm. You walk on, everybody pretending not to guess each other's wishes. Everybody is guessing.

variants.text: You whisper a wish into a pebble, so quietly that the mountain has to lean in to hear it. For a moment it feels warm. You walk on and keep the wish to yourself. That is what secret wishes are for.

choices.label: Climb on

choice_cairn_snack.narration: You set your very last snack on the cairn, wrapped up neatly, for whoever climbs up next. Your stomachs grumble about it all the way up. But someday somebody tired is going to find a snack on top of a mountain.

choices.label: Climb on, hungry and pleased

choice_cairn_big_names.narration: You carve your names as big as they will go. They go very big. Then you run out of stone, and the last name has to go around the back and up the side, and one letter ends up on a different stone altogether. Climbers for years will read it and wonder who on earth MAGNIFICEN was. It is still, honestly, very impressive.

choices.label: Climb on, magnificently

choice_cairn_oldest.narration: The oldest stone is right at the bottom, its name worn almost smooth. You trace it with a finger. It is not a name you know. But under it someone scratched a tiny drawing: a dragon, a round window, and a little stick figure waving. Somebody climbed up here a very, very long time ago, for the same reason you did. You set your pebble right beside it.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_bell_hut.narration: Just below the summit is the highest bell-hut in the foothills, where the dragonlings start the bell-code on its way down. It is empty. The rope is tied to a hook with a note: TIED SO NOBODY RINGS THE LAST ONE BY ACCIDENT. There is just enough slack for an ordinary ring.

variants.text: Your packs are so light up here that you could almost run. The wind tugs at them, finds only rush gems and crumbs, and goes away puzzled.
Up here, your packs hum louder than ever: {facets} of the great stones, carried all this way.
Up here, every step is heavier. You have carried {facets} great stones nearly to the top, and the bell rope sways, though there is no wind.

choices.label: Ring the all's well, for everyone below
Leave it be, and tie a second knot to be sure
Ring it properly, the way your family does

check_bell_code.narration: Inside the hut, the all's well code is painted on a card, but a mouse has nibbled it into scraps. Put the rings back in the right order, and then pull the rope.

interaction.cue: Share the scraps, then choose the rings in order.
clues: The code starts with two long rings.
One short ring sits right in the middle.
It ends with two long rings, the same as the start.

onSuccess.narration: Two long, one short, two long. Exactly right. The ring rolls down the mountain, and hut after hut rings it back: all's well. It is not quite true yet. It is a promise.

onFailure.narration: Two long, one short? Or one short, two long? You ring it anyway. Far below, the next hut pauses. Then it rings it back, and the next, and the next. It is not all's well. It is something else entirely.

onAssisted.narration: You lay the scraps side by side and the code comes clear. Two long, one short, two long. The ring rolls down the mountain, and hut after hut rings it back: all's well. It is not quite true yet. It is a promise.

scene_soup_ring.narration: It is the soup's ready ring. All the way down the mountain, every bell-hut is now cheerfully ringing soup's ready. Thousands of frightened people stop running for a moment and think about soup. Honestly, that might be better than all's well.

choices.label: Climb on, still giggling

scene_bell_hut_knot.narration: You tie a second knot, a good one, and then a third, because three is a nice number. As you leave, the old hut creaks in the wind, as if it had been worrying about that rope all day and can finally stop.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_bell_hut_family.narration: You ring it the family way: two long, one short, two long, with the little flick at the end that only grandmothers bother with. The ring rolls down the mountain, and the huts below answer one by one: all's well. Then one very far hut adds a flick at the end, just like yours. Somebody down there knows exactly who is ringing.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_crab_field.narration: The path crosses a field of gray ash covered in big, glittering gems. Except every so often, a gem blinks. They are glassback crabs, hundreds of them, pretending to be a gem deposit so nobody will dig them up. It is not a very good plan. Several are waving their claws at you.

choices.label: Read their claw-waving, and walk where they say
Hop around the crumbly edge of the field
Out-pretend them with an even better act
Let them hear your collection, and see what happens

check_crab_field.prompt: Read what the glassback crabs are waving about

onSuccess.narration: Claw up means not here. Claw sideways means go on. You read them like a signpost and walk a wiggly line across, and not one crab gets stepped on.

onFailure.narration: You read go on where it clearly said absolutely not, and step on a crab. It is not hurt, only very offended, and it holds onto your bootlace all the way across like a ticket.

check_crab_edge.prompt: Hop from rock to rock around the crumbly edge of the ash field

onSuccess.narration: You hop from rock to rock, quick as a sparrow. The whole field of crabs shuffles sideways to keep an eye on you, glittering, like the world's most suspicious audience.

onFailure.narration: A rock rolls, and you sit down hard in the ash. A hundred crabs turn to stare. One pats your boot, very kindly, as if you were a new and slightly broken gem. You get up and keep going, dusty.

scene_crab_field_glitter.narration: You crouch down, go perfectly still, and glitter. Somehow, you glitter. The crabs stare. One by one they decide you are a much better gem deposit than they are, and they shuffle aside in deep professional jealousy. You cross the whole field one sparkly step at a time. Nobody will ever believe this. You are going to tell it anyway.

choices.label: Climb on, sparkling

scene_crab_field_collection.narration: You open your pack a crack, and the collection hums. Every crab in the field stops pretending. Hundreds of tiny eyes turn to stare at your pack, as if they have just met the biggest gem deposit in the world, and it is walking. They part to let you through without a single wave. You are not sure that was respect. It felt a little like being a mountain.

variants.text: You open your pack a crack, and your few rush gems hum. The crabs stop pretending, just for a moment, and stare. Then they look at each other, and you can almost hear them thinking: is that it? They part to let you through anyway, the way you make room for somebody small. It is not respect, exactly. It is a little bit like kindness.
Behind you, the whole ash field sinks a finger's width, as if {facets} great stones walking across it were more than it could quite hold.

choices.label: Climb on

scene_ember_drift.narration: Near the top, something tiny glows in a drift of ash: one embermoth, stuck up to its wings, blinking like a nightlight running low. Every moth out here has flown away from the mountain, except the old ones deep inside it. This one looks up at you like a lost puppy.

choices.label: Dig it out, carefully, with your hands
Scoop it up, ash and all, and carry it with you
Hold the Ember Facet close, so it can find the warm
Use the tiny woven broom someone left by the drift

check_ember_drift.prompt: Dig the embermoth out of the ash without squashing it

onSuccess.narration: You dig gently, like digging out a sandcastle you want to keep. The moth pops free, shakes off the ash, and zooms ahead up the path, glowing brighter every second.

onFailure.narration: You dig too fast, and ash flies everywhere, mostly up your nose. While you sneeze, the moth wriggles out by itself, gives you a very dignified look, and flies off uphill.

scene_ember_drift_carry.narration: You scoop it up, ash and all. It is warm, like the last bit of a campfire, and slowly it glows a little brighter. Your pack rides high on your back, and the moth rides in your cupped hands the rest of the way up.

choices.label: Climb on, carrying it

scene_ember_drift_ember.narration: You hold the Ember Facet close to the drift, your very first stone. The moth crawls out of the ash and straight onto it, as if it had been looking for exactly this all along. It curls up on the warm stone like a cat on a hearth and goes to sleep. So now you are carrying it up the mountain too. You do not mind one bit.

choices.label: Climb on, carrying it

scene_ember_drift_broom.narration: Leaning on a rock by the drift is a broom no bigger than your finger, woven out of straw, with a tiny medal on it that says HELP. Nobody is around. Nobody ever is, when the sprites are being kind. You sweep the moth free in three neat strokes, and it flies off uphill ahead of you, glowing. When you look back, the broom is gone.

choices.label: Climb on

choice_last_breath.narration: At the very top, the path ends at a dark round hole: a lava tube, breathing warm air out at you, slow and steady, like something asleep. The stones in your packs hum so loudly you feel it in your teeth. Everybody vote: what do we do with our last minute outside?

choices.label: Tell each other the best bit of the whole road
Count the great stones, one more time
Count what you did bring
Practice what you will say when you give them back
Polish the collection until it shines in the dark
Check the tether one last time

choice_last_breath_best.narration: You tell each other the best bit of the whole road. Nobody picks the same one. Somebody picks a thing so small that everybody had forgotten it, and everybody laughs. Most of the best bits were the soggy bits.

variants.text: You tell the best bit out loud, to the mountain, since it is the only one here to listen. Then another, and another, and you laugh at one so small you had almost forgotten it. Most of the best bits were the soggy bits.

choices.label: Go in

choice_last_breath_count.narration: You tip the stones out on a flat rock and count them one more time. They hum together, like a choir warming up. You remember where every one came from, and who was there. Then you pack them away, carefully.

variants.text: You tip out your one great stone and look at it one more time. It hums a small, steady note. You remember the day you found it, and who was there. Then you pack it away, carefully.
You tip out the great stones and count them one more time: {facets}. They hum together like a very small choir. You remember where every one came from. Then you pack them away, carefully.

You tip out the great stones and count them out loud: {facets}. The rock creaks under them, and far below, the mountain hums along, as if it has been counting too. Then you pack them away. They are very heavy.

choices.label: Go in

choice_last_breath_count_brought.narration: You turn out your pockets on a flat rock: a few rush gems, some crumbs, a bit of string. Then you count the things that do not fit in pockets: the people who waved you on, the promises you made, the friends waiting at home. That count takes the whole minute.

choices.label: Go in

choice_last_breath_practice.narration: You practice what you will say when you give the stones back. "Here you are." Too short. "We are very sorry about the whole entire rush." Too long. "These are yours." That one is right. You say it out loud, three times, until it sounds like you mean it. You do mean it. That was never the hard part.

choices.label: Go in

choice_last_breath_polish.narration: You polish every stone in the collection on your sleeves until they shine, even in the shadow of the tube. Laid out on the rock, they glow in a rough circle, with one space left at the top. Nobody says anything about the space. Everybody looks at it. Then you pack them up and go in to find what fills it.

variants.text: You polish what you have on your sleeves: a few rush gems, the ordinary humming kind. Laid out on the rock, they make a very small circle with a great deal of space in it. Nobody says anything about the space. Everybody looks at it. Then you pack them up and go in, to see what a collection with nothing in it can still do.

choices.label: Go in

choice_last_breath_tether.narration: You check the tether one last time: what you borrowed, what you promised, what you made up on the way. It is all there, or most of it is. You tie a knot in the last bit of string you have, for luck. It is not a leash. It might be the start of one. It is going to have to do.

choices.label: Go in

scene_mouth.narration: You step into the lava tube. It opens into a gallery where the walls glitter with gem-veins, like fireworks frozen halfway through going off. Then the old bones in the rock begin, very slowly, to stand up. They are not looking at you. They are looking at your pockets.

variants.text: There is not much in your pockets but rush gems and crumbs. The bones look anyway, puzzled, the way a dog sniffs an empty hand.
Along the walls, the gem-veins light up one after another as you pass, following your packs. You carry {facets} great stones, and the whole gallery has noticed.

choices.label: Help the bones lie back down, gently
Stand your ground
Set the Table Stone back into the vein
Set the Ember Facet back into the wall
Follow the embermoths down a cool side tunnel
Stop. Listen. Is that... bells?

scene_mouth_ember_back.narration: You press the Ember Facet into the wall, your very first stone, warm as toast all the way from the Exchange gutter. It fits. Of course it fits. The vein takes it with a sound like a sigh, and the bones sink back into the rock as if somebody had finally said the thing they were waiting to hear. Then the wall warms and nudges the stone back out into your hand, gently, as if to say: not here. Further down.

choices.label: Go on down

scene_mouth_table_back.narration: You set the Table Stone into the nearest gem-vein, and it slides in as if it had been missing exactly that long. The wall glows brighter along the whole vein, like a lamp being turned up. The bones stop, consider this, and lie back down one by one, very carefully, the way you put down something you had been meaning to put down for years. Then the vein pushes the stone back into your palm, the way you hand back something borrowed. Further down, it seems to say.

choices.label: Go on down

scene_moth_road.narration: The embermoths have not given up on this mountain yet. They lead you down a side tunnel where the rock is cool enough to touch, and one of them rides on your nose the whole way, like a tiny glowing hat. Behind you, the bones sit back down. Nobody was in a hurry, so nobody had to be.

choices.label: Follow the moths all the way

scene_bells_first.narration: Far behind you, down in the foothills, the bells are ringing. Ordinary rings, every town at once, one after another. Nobody has rung the last one yet. But everybody is standing right next to it. Halfway out of the wall, one of the bones stops to listen too, with a bony hand cupped behind where its ear used to be.

choices.label: Help the bones back down, gently
Stand your ground

check_remains.prompt: Walk the bones back to their places in the wall, one gentle step at a time

onSuccess.narration: You take a bony hand, very gently, and walk it back to its place, like walking a sleepwalker back to bed. The others follow. One of them nods, which is a lot of nodding for a bone.

onFailure.narration: You reach for the nearest bony hand, but the stones in your pockets hum louder than you can be gentle. The bones slip past you and keep walking toward the hum.

encounter_gallery.narration: The restless remains clatter across the glittering floor, walking toward whatever is wrong. Right now, what is wrong is you. One of them has lost a toe bone and keeps stopping to look for it.

onVictory.narration: The bones sink back into the rock, tired and a bit relieved, as if they never wanted to do that either.

onDefeat.narration: The bones do not hurt you. They just carry you, gently and very slowly, all the way back up the tube to where you started. By the time you climb back down, the bells have started counting down.

rest_cool_gallery.narration: A side gallery where the air is cool and the gem-veins glow just bright enough to read by. Embermoths are dusting the walls, and one has missed a spot. Eat what you have left, patch your scrapes, and listen to the mountain breathing below. It is breathing faster.

choices.label: Down toward the heat
Take the moths' slow, cool road all the way down

check_race_1.prompt: Race the shaking floor down the last long tube

onSuccess.narration: You run, jump, slide, and arrive at the bottom in a heap. But it is an on-time heap.

onFailure.narration: A tremor knocks you flat, and the tube fills with ash-dust. When it clears, you can hear the bells, all the way from the foothills.

scene_bells_ringing.narration: Every bell in the foothills is ringing now, one ring after another, counting down toward the ring nobody uses. The floor jumps with every one, and a loose pebble bounces down the tube in time, as if it is trying to help count. Five rings left. Maybe four.

scene_keeper.narration: At the bottom of the mountain is a cave as big as the sky, and in it is the Seal-Keeper: a dragon so old its scales have turned to gemstone at the edges. An embermoth snores on the tip of its nose. It has guarded the seal since before the realm had a name, and nobody reaches the seal without answering it. "What did you carry up my mountain?" it asks. It already knows.

"Everyone who climbs my mountain brings me stones," it says. "Or excuses for stones. Nobody has ever brought me nothing on purpose." An embermoth crawls off its nose and onto your shoulder. choices.label: Hear the next question

choices.label: Hear the next question

choices.label: Hear the next question

choices.label: Hear the next question

scene_keeper_truth.narration: You tell it the truth: every stone, where it came from, and who was there. The Seal-Keeper listens without moving at all. "Yes," it says, as if checking your answer against a very old list. "That is what you carried."

variants.text: You tell it the truth: a few rush gems, like everybody's, and nothing else. Then you tell it what else you carried: the road, the people on it, a promise or two. "Yes," says the Seal-Keeper. "That is lighter than most. It is not less."

choices.label: Hear the next question

choices.label: Hear the next question

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_q2_forded.narration: "We forded the west branch," you say. "Clean across." "How?" asks the Seal-Keeper, so you tell it, and somewhere in the telling you start to hum, and it hums along, badly, under its breath, as if it has not sung in a long time.

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_q2_river_took.narration: "The river took us," you say. "Old Ossley fished us out." The Seal-Keeper's head comes up. "Ossley," it says, and for the first time it sounds surprised. "He does not fish out everybody." It looks at you again, more carefully, as if Ossley's opinion is one it takes seriously.

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_q2_crossed_dry.narration: "Old Lintel heard our toll stories all the way through," you say. The Seal-Keeper makes a sound that might be a laugh and might be a rockfall. "Lintel," it says. "He used to ask riddles himself, you know. He only stops when he is worried." It seems to find this very interesting.

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_q2_glade_finished.narration: "We took the Glade Stone," you say. "The glade is healing slowly." The Seal-Keeper does not say anything for a long time. "Slowly," it says at last. "Yes. It would be." The embermoth on its eyebrow folds its wings.

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_q2_glade_mended.narration: "The wounded glade is green again," you say. The Seal-Keeper closes its eyes. When it opens them, the gem-veins in the walls have gone a soft green for a moment, like moss remembering its color. "I felt that," it says. "From here." It looks at you as if it is memorizing something.

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_q2_road.narration: You tell it what happened: the good bits, the soggy bits, the bits you are not proud of. The Seal-Keeper listens to all of it without interrupting. "Yes," it says at the end. "That is a road." It does not say whether it was a good one.

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_q2_people.narration: You tell it about the people who lent you rope, and pointed the way, and fed you soup that was only soup. The Seal-Keeper listens with its head on one side. "People," it says, trying the word out. "They do keep turning up." It does not sound annoyed.

choices.label: Hear the last question

scene_verdict.narration: "Last question," says the Seal-Keeper. "Who did you tell? And what do you want?" Under the floor, something huge turns over in its sleep, and the whole cave rocks like a boat. Somewhere in the wall, a bone sneezes. Everybody pretends not to notice.

scene_verdict_honest.narration: You tell it what you want, as honestly as you can, even the parts that sound silly out loud. The Seal-Keeper listens all the way to the end without blinking once. "Honest," it says. "Up here, that is rarer than gems." Then it waits, to see whether you meant it.

"They write everything down twice," it says. "I have read their logs. They are very good at noticing, and not so good at climbing. You climbed." Then it waits, to see whether you meant it.

choices.label: Hold its gaze while it decides

scene_verdict_close.narration: "We told nobody," you say. "We came ourselves." The Seal-Keeper tilts its enormous head, and three embermoths slide off its nose. "Then nobody will thank you," it says, "and nobody will come to help. Can you bear that?" It waits for your answer, and it is in no hurry at all.

choices.label: Hold its gaze while it decides

scene_verdict_rich.narration: "Honestly?" you say. "We came to get rich." There is a long pause. Then the Seal-Keeper makes a sound like a rockslide, which turns out to be a laugh. "At last," it says. "Everybody else says they came for me." Then it looks at you, very hard, to see what else is in there.

choices.label: Hold its gaze while it decides

scene_verdict_duty.narration: "Somebody had to come," you say. "So we came." The Seal-Keeper is quiet for a long time. "Somebody," it says. "I have been somebody for a very long time. It is heavy." An embermoth lands on your shoulder, as if to help carry it. Then the dragon waits, to see whether you meant it.

choices.label: Hold its gaze while it decides

scene_verdict_proving.narration: "We came to find out if we could," you say. "And can you?" asks the Seal-Keeper. You do not know yet, and you say so. It nods, slowly, so slowly that a moth on its eyebrow has time to fall asleep. "Then we will both find out," it says, and waits.

choices.label: Hold its gaze while it decides

scene_verdict_gatherers.narration: "We told the grandmothers," you say, "and they told everyone." The Seal-Keeper's breath goes out in a long warm rush, and every embermoth in the cave rises and settles again. "The grandmothers," it says. "They have been telling everyone for a thousand years." It moves aside. "Finally," it says, "somebody listened."

choices.label: Step up to the seal

scene_verdict_surprised.narration: Something in its eyes has changed, and you wait for it. The Seal-Keeper lowers its head until one eye is level with you. "I am very rarely surprised," it says. "Twice in a thousand years, before today." It moves aside, slowly, the way a hill would move aside if it chose to.

choices.label: Step up to the seal

onFailure.narration: The dragon sighs. The sigh is warm, and not the good kind of warm. "Then show me," it says.

encounter_dragon.narration: The Seal-Keeper uncurls until it fills the cave, and an old guardian of bones steps out of the wall to stand beside it, looking extremely pleased to be included.

onVictory.narration: The dragon lowers its head and laughs, a sound like an avalanche having a nice day. "You fight like people who mean it," it says, and steps aside.

onDefeat.narration: The Seal-Keeper scoops you up in one enormous claw, very carefully, the way you would carry a bird's nest.

variants.text: You are the only one in there, and the claw is big enough for twenty. It is warm, and it holds still, and somehow it is the least alone you have felt all day.

scene_dragon_claw.narration: It lifts you up to one enormous eye, gently, the way you would lift a ladybug to get a proper look at it. "You came up my mountain the wrong way," it says. "What do you have left to give?"

onFailure.narration: Your fingers slip. The Seal-Keeper does not drop you. It only holds you up, very patiently, and waits.

scene_dragon_claw_slip.narration: "Well?" asks the Seal-Keeper. Behind it the seal creaks, and the thing underneath turns over again. "What do you have left?"

Ask it for the time to do this right

"Better," it says, and puts you down in front of the seal. That stone is the mountain's again, and it is not coming back.

When it finally lets you up, the mountain is shaking harder than before. "Now," it says. "Look."

scene_titan_eye.narration: Under the glass, something opens: an eye as big as a pond, the color of the red sky at sunset. It looks up at you, slow and sleepy. Then the old, old note the stones have always hummed comes up through the floor, and every rush gem in your pockets hums with it.

onAssisted.narration: The Seal-Keeper hums the first note beside you, soft as a cat's purr, and you follow it, one hum at a time. The great eye blinks, slowly. The note comes back, like a sleepy friend answering from under the covers. The shaking eases. It heard you.

check_hear_titan.narration: You press your ear to the warm glass. The sounds arrive in pieces, one at a time, and every piece is part of the same question. Share what everyone hears, then put the sounds in order.

interaction.cue: Share what you hear, then choose the sounds in order.
clues: It starts with the low rumble.
The chime comes just before the sigh.

onSuccess.narration: It is not one note. It is a question, the same few sounds over and over, the way a little kid asks the same thing at bedtime. The Seal-Keeper nods. "Yes," it says. "You hear it too."

onFailure.narration: All you hear is a hum that makes your ear itch. Then the Seal-Keeper lowers its head beside you. "It is asking something," it says. "It always asks the same thing."

onAssisted.narration: The Seal-Keeper lowers its head beside you and listens too. Rumble, chime, sigh, over and over, the way a little kid asks the same thing at bedtime. "Yes," it says. "You hear it too."

scene_seal_chamber.narration: Here is the whole truth, plain at last. Every gemstone the mountain ever threw out is a piece of the seal, and under the seal sleeps the titan, older than the mountain's name. The seal is its blanket. Every stone carried off let the cold in, and now it is waking. It is not angry. It is asking, and the Seal-Keeper says it out loud: "Is it morning? Should I get up?" On top of the seal sits the crown stone, bigger than your head, holding it all together. "I always answered for it," says the Keeper. "Today it asked you."

variants.text: You look at the gaps in the seal, and then at your empty hands. Whatever you answer, you will answer with what you brought, which is {party}.
In your packs, {facets} of the great stones tug toward the gaps, like a dog on a lead that has smelled home.
Your packs pull toward the gaps so hard you have to plant your feet. All {facets} great stones want to go home.

Reach for the crown stone at the top

onFailure.narration: The seal bucks, and everybody bounces. But you keep your hands on it, and slowly the Keeper's warm breath sets the cracks like toffee.

scene_restore_last_gap.narration: One gap is left, right under the crown stone. The titan's eye is nearly shut now, but it is still watching, the way you watch the door at bedtime. "Something to finish it," says the Seal-Keeper. "Anything given on purpose will do."

choices.label: Fill it with every rush gem in your pockets
Hum the old note slow, like a lullaby
Set Tansy's little stone in it, with her sorry

scene_restore_last_gap_gems.narration: You turn out every pocket. Rush gems pour into the gap, little ordinary ones, the kind everybody carries. They should not be enough. But they fill it right to the top, humming, and the whole seal shines.

choices.label: Watch the eye

scene_restore_last_gap_little_stone.narration: You set Tansy's little pink stone in the gap and say her sorry out loud. It fits exactly. Of course it does. The titan's eye crinkles, just a little, as if it has been waiting all day for somebody to say sorry.

choices.label: Watch the eye

onSuccess.narration: You hum, slow and soft. The great eye droops, and droops, and the last gap fills with light all by itself, like a window when somebody inside lights a lamp.

onFailure.narration: You yawn halfway through, which is not very helpful. But yawns are catching. The titan yawns too, a warm wind that blows your hair straight back, and the last gap fills with light.

scene_titan_sleeps.narration: The great eye closes, slowly, like a sunset. A long warm sigh blows through the cave and tumbles every embermoth head over heels. choices.label: Walk out the front, into the bells
Stay a while and watch it sleep

onSuccess.narration: It comes loose with a sound like a cork from the biggest bottle in the world. You did not come up here for this. You are holding it anyway.

onFailure.narration: The crown stone does not budge. It is hot as an oven door, and your hands sting. Then the Seal-Keeper puts one claw on it, very gently, and the decision is no longer yours.

scene_keystone_refused.narration: The Seal-Keeper lifts your hands off the crown stone one finger at a time, like somebody unsticking a starfish from a rock. "Not that one," it says. "Not today, and not by you." It sets you back in front of the seal. The crown stone stays exactly where it is, and so does the claw.

choices.label: Choose again, with stinging hands

scene_keystone_lifted.narration: The crown stone comes free in your arms, warm as a sleeping cat. The whole seal shudders. Under the glass, the great eye flies open, bright and wide awake. Then the Seal-Keeper lies down across the seal, slow as a hill, and stays there. "Go," it says. "I will hold the door. I will always hold the door."

choices.label: Carry the Keystone out of the mountain

interaction_bundles.narration: Down the slope, the faun family has stopped again. Their goat has parked the cart across a washed-out step, and it will not budge. Tansy's father waves both arms at you. "Help us pass the bundles over the gap, hand to hand!" he calls. "Quick, before the goat has opinions!"

interaction.cue: Catch the bundle, then pass it along.

onSuccess.narration: Bundle after bundle goes over the gap, and not one lands in the mud. The goat watches the whole thing, chewing. Tansy's mother presses a warm honeycake into your hands. "For the climb," she says, "and for being nice to my small one."

onFailure.narration: One bundle bursts open, and a whole pillow's worth of feathers floats down the mountain like snow. The goat sneezes. The family laughs, and the cart rolls on.

onAssisted.narration: Together you and Tansy's father pass the bundles in a slow, steady row, and not one lands in the mud. Tansy's mother presses a warm honeycake into your hands. "For the climb," she says.

scene_warden_post_tin.narration: The coin goes in with a clink. The tin rattles, and the lid pops open. Inside is a brave whistle on a string, with a tag: FOR A LOUD MOMENT. Somebody has been saving these for climbers who pay it forward. You sign the log too, in small letters, just under the last name.

choices.label: Climb on

interaction_chimney.narration: Above the wardens' post, the stair gives out into a steep chimney of warm rock. A rope hangs down it, and a sign says: ONE CLIMBER AT A TIME. EVERYBODY ELSE HOLDS THE ROPE. THIS MEANS YOU TOO. The top is very high, and very close to the clouds.

interaction.cue: Friends hold the rope steady while someone climbs.

onSuccess.narration: Hand over hand, up you go, and the rope never wobbles once. You pop out over the lip of the chimney with your hair full of cloud.

onFailure.narration: The rope swings, and you slide down on your bottom to the nearest ledge. You try again from the side, the long way round. It takes longer, but you pop out over the lip with your hair full of cloud.

onAssisted.narration: Everybody holds the rope together, and you climb one slow hand at a time. You pop out over the lip of the chimney with your hair full of cloud.

scene_crab_guards.narration: On the far side of the field, the two biggest crabs have beaten you to the path. They must have taken a shortcut under the ash. They plant themselves in the only way up, claws raised. They are the field's guards, and they have decided that anybody who crossed their gem field must be a digger. Crabs cannot be argued with. They can, however, be bumped. Gently, with a shoulder, until they get the idea.

choices.label: Shoulder the guard crabs off the path

encounter_crabs.narration: The guard crabs click and clack and puff out their glassy backs. They only want you off their field. Bump them off the path before they bump you back.

scene_crabs_bumped.narration: The guard crabs go over like two upside-down teacups, and then right themselves, very offended. Then the oldest one clacks its claws and scuttles aside. Under the spot where it sat is a small pile of things diggers dropped long ago: three coins, and a smooth, lucky-looking stone. The crab pushes them toward you with one claw. You are, it seems, climbers after all.

choices.label: Thank them and climb on

scene_crabs_herded.narration: The crabs shoulder you back and forth until you are sitting in the ash, dizzy and a little giggly. Then they march around you in a circle, clicking, and herd you off their field and onto the path, the way a sheepdog would. The oldest crab pats your boot. Nobody is hurt. You get a rest in the ash, and a good look at the sky.

choices.label: Dust off and climb on

interaction_climb_warmup.narration: At the foot of the last climb, cold wind makes your fingers stiff. Take a moment to wake up hands and feet. A mountain this tall deserves your best stomping boots.

interaction.cue: Warm up before the mountain climb.

options.label: Stamp your boots
options.reaction: Loose grit dances around your feet.

options.label: Stretch up high
options.reaction: The summit still looks very far away.

options.label: Shake out your hands
options.reaction: Your fingers feel ready for the rocks.
